business_summary: Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE) is an exchange and clearing-house holding company. It holds two sourced roles on this chain: prediction-market-venue, via an October 2025 strategic investment of up to USD 2 billion in Polymarket and a global Polymarket event-driven-data distribution role, and clearing-and-collateral, via its own six clearing houses (ICE Clear Europe, ICE Clear U.S., ICE Clear Credit and others).

exposure_summary.narrative: ICE holds two sourced roles on prediction-market-plumbing: prediction-market-venue (CROWDED, chain position 7, via the Polymarket investment) and clearing-and-collateral (EMERGING, position 8, via its own clearing-house network, a separate business from the Polymarket stake). FY2025 revenue was USD 12,640.0M (9.5% three-year CAGR) with a 39.0% operating margin and net income of USD 3,315.0M. Net debt to EBITDA is 2.71x. Piotroski and Beneish are both PENDING_DATA this run: companyfacts is missing cost_of_revenue_fy for this filer (8/9 and 10/12 inputs found, beneish also missing ppe_net_fy).

crowdedness_caveats: prediction-market-venue is scored CROWDED, not EMERGING: the chain notes five listed issuers (ICE via Polymarket, DraftKings via Railbird, IBKR via ForecastEx, CME via FanDuel, Cboe via an options wrapper) have already reached this seat, and the two largest venues by volume, Kalshi and Polymarket, are private, which the chain calls the crowdedness trap on this link.

ICE's prediction-market-venue exposure is an investment stake and data-distribution role in a private company (Polymarket), not a wholly-owned venue the way Cboe's Mini-SPX or DraftKings' Railbird acquisition are.
